analysis.investment_thesis: Blue Dart trades at 44x earnings and 7.8x book, while its net profit CAGR over 9 years is a mere 2.8% — investors are paying a growth premium for a business that has not grown earnings materially. My Graham Number of approximately ₹1,284 against a market price of ₹5,391 represents a 4.2x premium with no margin of safety.
key_strengths: Dominant premium logistics brand with DHL Group backing and a fleet of 8 Boeing freighters — genuine operational moat in Indian express delivery
5/5 years positive OCF with free cash flow consistently above ₹400 Cr in recent years — cash conversion is real
Revenue has grown from ₹2,563 Cr (FY2016) to ₹5,720 Cr (FY2025) at a 9.3% CAGR — steady topline expansion
key_risks: Net profit peaked at ₹382 Cr in FY2022 and has declined every year since to ₹252 Cr in FY2025 — a 34% earnings decline while valuation remains elevated
Debt of ₹1,008 Cr versus equity of ₹1,632 Cr gives a D/E of ~0.62, above my 0.5 limit, and finance costs have structurally risen since FY2020
Net loss in FY2020 (–₹42 Cr) demonstrates earnings fragility — a single disruption year wiped out all profit
red_flags: 9-year net profit CAGR of 2.8% is barely ahead of inflation — this is not a growth business at 44x earnings
EBITDA has been contracting (trend: contracting per 5-year data) while the stock commands a premium multiple — deteriorating fundamentals with rising price
Subsidiary of DHL Singapore — minority shareholders may not fully benefit from strategic decisions made in favour of the parent
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Graham Number: EPS ~₹106 and BVPS ~₹689 yields approximately ₹1,284. At ₹5,391, the market is pricing in a logistics franchise transformation that the income statement simply does not support. Net profit has fallen three years running: ₹382 Cr (FY2022), ₹371 Cr (FY2023), ₹301 Cr (FY2024), ₹252 Cr (FY2025). A stock with declining earnings should be selling at a discount, not a 44x multiple.

The business itself — premium courier with proven brand — has genuine moat characteristics, but I distinguish between a good business and a good investment. The DHL parent ownership creates structural agency risk for minority shareholders, as pricing, capital allocation, and strategic decisions may favour the group over listed shareholders. At ₹1,200–1,400 (near Graham Number range), this becomes interesting; at ₹5,391, the disciplined investor must look elsewhere.
